A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gumiho research. The main text and Appendices A-D are readable and matchable, including equations, figures and tables, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding-speed and token-acceptance experiments, architectural ablations, A100 evaluations in Appendix B, and head-accuracy comparisons in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds measured execution times for individual pipeline components in Table 3.

M1.justification: The reused two-layer Transformer generating the first two tokens, five parallel MLPs, FTA mechanism and training objective remain unchanged. The expanded setup description repeats token allocation already documented in v1 Section 3.3 and Figure 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use ShareGPT training and the same six evaluation datasets: MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca, CNN/Daily Mail and Natural Questions. The added timing breakdown introduces no new task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Medusa, Hydra, Eagle and Eagle-2 participation for each model and temperature setting, including Appendix B. Cerberus is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds component-level wall-clock measurements alongside the existing aggregate timing and speedup evaluation. This extends measurement granularity; the retained model configurations, temperatures, hardware and training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new runtime breakdown examines where execution time is spent across drafting, FTA, other computation and verification. Existing depth, width, FTA-removal and Appendix D head-accuracy analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added timing table likewise provides point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports 2.80 and 3.46 ms for the serial heads, 2.02 ms for parallel heads, 3.41 ms for FTA, 6.11 ms for other computation and 45.50 ms for verification. Existing benchmark and ablation results, including appendix results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The acceptance-probability assumptions, Theorem 3.1, mathematical definitions and detailed Appendix A proof are unchanged. No new theoretical result or mathematical correction appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: prioritizing early tokens, combining serial and parallel heads, introducing FTA, and outperforming existing decoding methods. The added timing evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New Section 6 acknowledges that the larger draft model requires more GPU memory during training than architectures such as Eagle and Medusa, attributing this to the jointly trained Transformer and five MLP heads. Existing result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and Gumiho repository URL in the abstract. Appendix C's implementation details and hyperparameters are unchanged; the PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Cerberus by Liu et al. (2024b) to the self-drafting literature. This is a limited citation addition without a substantial revision of the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds short timing and limitations passages, expands the setup explanation, corrects minor wording, and updates affiliation labels and publication information. Most prose and the existing section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the compact component-timing Table 3 and locally reflows the conclusion and references. Appendix tables 3 and 4 become Tables 4 and 5; all six existing figures and retained table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Table 3 makes computational costs more transparent, Section 6 explicitly acknowledges the training-memory tradeoff, and the abstract supplies code-access information. These useful, bounded additions improve practical assessability while the method, proof and existing empirical evidence remain unchanged.
